category: Usenet binary search engine (HTML search, anonymous NZB build)

free_tier.stated: No account and no key. GET /search?q=linux returned 98,890 bytes of results, paginated to 174 pages. GET /nzb?q=linux&<base64 collection id>=on returned a 4,229-byte NZB carrying 9 files. The site publishes no daily counter anywhere a reader can reach.
free_tier.notes: 'unlimited' is a statement about the absence of a published quota, supported by a 6-request burst, not by a vendor sentence.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the answer is an NZB pointer file (4,229 bytes, 9 files), never the payload

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read. A third-party indexer comparison claims 'up to 1,100 days of binary retention, searches 400+ popular newsgroups by default' (nzbhydra.com, 2026-10-23).
retention.notes: reported, not documented: Binsearch publishes no retention figure on its search or results page.

egress.terms: No metering. Every answer is a small XML pointer file; the bytes themselves come from whichever news provider a user holds an account with.

interface_detail: HTML search over HTTP GET against /search (Next.js front end, results server-rendered). NZB is built by a GET to /nzb?q=<query>&<name>=on where <name> is the base64 collection id carried by each result's checkbox. There is no Newznab endpoint: /api returns 404.
tooling: No Newznab API, so Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr and NZBHydra2 cannot add it as an indexer. A wrapper must GET /search, parse the collection ids out of the checkbox names, and re-issue GET /nzb. Two GETs per download.
chaining: A fallback name search when every Newznab indexer is down or refuses registration; the NZB it returns goes into the same SABnzbd or NZBGet queue as any other.

limits.value: none observed: 6 consecutive anonymous searches in one session all returned 200

limits_note: Page depth is the only ceiling the service shows: the query 'linux' exposed 174 pages. No per-IP shaping was observed and no quota page exists to read.
binding_note: Nothing in the seven-kind vocabulary fails at a client pulling 1 TiB a month: there is no counter to hit. The real cost is two GETs per NZB plus a scraper that survives a front-end rewrite, which is a tooling cost and not a limit.

identity_cost.detail: No account, no key, no cookie. Search and NZB creation both answered an anonymous request with no credential of any kind.

reliability_note: Advertiser-supported binary search engine; results are raw article headers, so completion depends entirely on the retention of the news provider a user pays, and dead posts stay listed until the indexer notices.
confidence_note: Search and NZB creation were both run today and both produced payload bytes with a recorded digest. Nothing here is quoted from a third party. What would raise nothing: the rung is already the top one; what is missing is a long-run rate test, which a 6-request burst does not provide.

evidence.proved: anonymous HTML search returned 200 and 98,890 bytes with 174 result pages and per-result collection ids
anonymous GET returned 200, a 4,229-byte NZB with 9 <file> elements (sha256 7070590f...)
the API path does not exist: 404, so there is no Newznab surface to add to a client
third-party claim of 1,100 days retention and 400+ groups; used only for the retention field, which Binsearch does not publish

notes: The result page is a Next.js front end but the results are server-rendered, so the HTML carries them; that is why a plain GET works where NZBIndex's does not.
